title: Standard constructible cohomology and open–closed restrictions at rational coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, put $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and let $C$ be a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme of pure dimension one. Use the finite-coefficient-field category $D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], for $T=C$ or a locally closed subscheme of $C$. Lisse sheaves have the meaning of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]; constructible sheaves are lisse on a finite locally closed stratification, and $\mathcal H^a$ denotes ordinary cohomology [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

The ordinary cohomological truncations restrict to a bounded t-structure on $D^b_c(T,\Lambda)$, with heart the constructible $\Lambda$-sheaves. This structure agrees with the ordinary cohomology of pro-étale $\Lambda_T$-module representatives, is compatible with finite extension of the coefficient field, and is preserved by scheme isomorphisms.

For a dense open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ with reduced closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$, the constructible pullbacks $j^*,i^*$ are t-exact, and on sheaves they jointly detect zero objects. Closed direct image $i_*$ is exact on sheaves and fully faithful, $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$, and its essential image on sheaves consists exactly of sheaves whose restriction to $U$ is zero. Open direct image $j_*$ on sheaves is right adjoint to $j^*$, with $j^*j_*\cong\mathrm{id}$, and sends lisse sheaves on $U$ to constructible sheaves on $C$. For $M\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$ with $\mathcal H^aM=0$ for $a<m$, one has
$$\mathcal H^a(Rj_*M)=0\ (a<m),\qquad \mathcal H^m(Rj_*M)\cong j_*\mathcal H^mM.$$
Under this identification and $\mathcal H^m(j^*K)=j^*\mathcal H^mK$, the degree-$m$ map induced by the derived unit $K\to Rj_*j^*K$, when $j^*K\in D^{\ge m}$, is the ordinary unit $\mathcal H^mK\to j_*j^*\mathcal H^mK$.

For a finite field $k_0$ and an immersion pair defined over $k_0$, these cohomology identifications, units, counits and truncation maps commute with the Frobenius isomorphisms of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] on the geometric fibers. No triangulated structure on that category of Frobenius pairs is asserted.
